# Paperlab

> Physical, realistic paper as a React component. A sheet is a real 3D mesh — content is a texture on geometry that genuinely bends, so text and images curl with perfect continuity. Preset-driven, serializable, agent-first.

Install: `npm i paperlab three @react-three/fiber gsap` (React ≥ 19, three ≥ 0.160)

## Core API

- `<Paper />` — one sheet, owns its own <Canvas>, fills its parent (parent needs a height!). Props: preset (name or object), sheet {width,height,thickness}, stock ('printer'|'thermal'|'kraft'|'newsprint'|'vellum'|'photo-gloss'|'sticker'), content ({type:'image',src,alt} | {type:'text',text,...} | {type:'receipt',store,items,...}), behavior, surface {grain,deckle,creaseLines,aging,perforation}, physics, interactive, autoplay, reducedMotion.
- `<PaperMesh />` — the same, canvas-less, for existing React Three Fiber scenes.
- `<PaperField />` — many sheets, one instanced draw call. Props: images | papers, preset, layout ('ring'|'fan'|'spread'|'pile'|'wall'|'spill'|'sheet'), layoutOptions, motion {driver:'autoplay'|'drag'|'none', speed}, entrance {type:'rise'|'scatter'|'none', stagger}. Layouts pose sheets AND set a per-sheet `bias` (0 = flat, 1 = as configured) so one draw call can bend each sheet differently. A `sheet` layout renders a stamp block on a shared backing; slots with `states` make the field interactive (per-paper hover/press/pick). `<DropZone id bounds={{position,size}} accept={['glob-*']} onPlace={(paper, zone) => …} />` children are drop targets for picked papers.
- Ref API: play(), pause(), set('progress', v), getProgress(), snapshot(), toJSON(), state, sendState(event).

## Behaviors (behavior={{ type, ...params }})

peel {progress, corner ('auto' resolves outward in a sheet field), radius} · unroll {progress, tightness, sway} · flip {progress, spine, radius} · letter-fold {progress, crease} · hang {wind, sag} · fly {flutter, curve} · fall {flutter, curl} · carry {grab, stiffness, flutter, lag, drive} (a held paper drooping from its pinch point) · flight {wind:[x,y,z], gustiness, tumble, path:'drift'|'loop', respawn, range} (free paper travelling across the scene)

## Physics

Idle (compose with behaviors): 'float' 'tumble' 'dangle' 'taped' 'breeze'. Cloth (exclusive with behavior — schema-enforced): physics={{type:'cloth', pins:'top-edge'|'top-corners'|'corner'|'none', wind, stiffness, gravity}}. Interactive cloth is grabbable.

## Presets

Built-ins: receipt-unroll, letter-fold, vintage-note, hero-peel, page-flip, hanging-poster, pinned-sheet, flying-note, blank-sheet, photo-print, typed-note, postage-stamp. Presets are .paper JSON validated by the exported zod paperConfigSchema; helpers: getPreset, parsePreset, serializePreset, diffConfig, buildAgentPayload, describeConfig.

## Interaction states (M6)

A preset may carry `states`: overrides-on-base diffs keyed rest/hover/pressed/picked/placed (`{states: {initial:'rest', states: {hover: {overrides: {behavior:{progress:0.4}}, transition: {duration:0.25, ease:'power2.out'}}}, pickThreshold: 0.08}}`). Triggers are built in: hover/press on pointer, drag past pickThreshold tears a stamp off its sheet (perforation edges facing neighbors flip to 'torn' automatically), release over a DropZone settles it (snap → press → flatten, then onPlace fires), release elsewhere flutters it back — torn stays torn. Field slots take a `states` override layer of their own. Keyboard flow ships automatically: focus a paper, Enter picks, arrows move between zones, Enter places, Esc returns.

## Pitfalls

1. Blank canvas = parent has no height (the classic R3F bug — <Paper> fills its parent).
2. cloth + behavior together throws by design: cloth owns the vertices.
3. prefers-reduced-motion freezes behaviors at their pose and disables physics/entrances automatically.
4. No WebGL → automatic flat DOM fallback; a hidden DOM mirror of the content always renders (use it for E2E assertions).

## Verify after integrating

Run the dev server; the exported describeConfig(config) returns the one-line visual you should see (e.g. 'a store receipt for "acme.dev" on thermal paper stock (1×2.6), unrolling from a paper roll at the bottom, torn (deckled) bottom edge').
